summary.text: A second-born female infant of consanguineous parents was born at 34 weeks of gestation after a pregnancy with intrauterine growth retardation and oligohydramnios. She was small for gestational age, admitted to the neonatology ward for feeding difficulties, and had mild hypokalemia with metabolic alkalosis that was not investigated further. She was discharged at 4 days of life without therapy.

At 7 months of age, because of failure to thrive, laboratory tests confirmed hypokalemia with metabolic alkalosis, now with low renin and aldosterone, and echocardiography was normal. A renal ultrasound raised suspicion of nephrocalcinosis and Bartter syndrome type III was suspected. At 9 months she was admitted to a pediatric nephrology unit for persistent growth failure; she had mild polyuria with low urine osmolality, a high urinary potassium to creatinine ratio and mild ventricular septal hypertrophy.

Over the following months polyuria worsened, urinary calcium rose and blood pressure was consistently elevated, and ventricular hypertrophy at 15 months led to antihypertensive therapy with little benefit. Liddle and Geller syndromes and congenital adrenal hyperplasia types IV and V were excluded, an elevated urinary THF + 5α-THF to THE ratio confirmed apparent mineralocorticoid excess syndrome, and sequencing found a homozygous HSD11B2 frameshift variant with heterozygous carrier parents.

A low sodium diet was started and spironolactone and amiloride were prescribed. Three months later blood pressure had improved and electrolytes and blood pH had normalized. At 30 months mild polyuria persisted; growth velocity had changed from its value at diagnosis. At 36 months the ventricular hypertrophy had regressed while nephrocalcinosis was unchanged.
